questions.question: Explain the difference between agent function and agent programme. Why should internal complexity not determine the evaluation?
questions.modelAnswer: The agent function maps percept sequences to actions and specifies what should be done for every possible history. It is potentially infinite. The programme is the finite implementation that approximates it and runs on an architecture. Evaluation concerns the actions selected rather than the complexity of the machinery choosing them.
rubric: Distinguish mathematical specification from implementation.
Mention percept sequences and potentially infinite histories.
Judge behaviour rather than internal complexity.
questions.hint2: The agent function maps percept sequences to actions and specifies what should be done for every possible history.

questions.question: Explain why rationality is neither omniscience nor perfection, using the falling-cargo example.
questions.modelAnswer: Rationality maximises expected performance given the available percept history and built-in knowledge; perfection maximises actual performance. Looking both ways before crossing may be rational even if falling cargo causes a bad outcome. Rationality also depends on the chosen performance measure and may require gathering information or learning when additional information is cheaply available.
rubric: Contrast expected and actual outcomes.
Apply available information to the cargo example.
Explain performance measure and information gathering.
questions.hint2: Rationality maximises expected performance given the available percept history and built-in knowledge; perfection maximises actual performance.

questions.question: Explain the vacuum's specification-gaming failure and repair its performance measure.
questions.modelAnswer: Rewarding dirt collected over eight hours encourages ejecting collected dirt and collecting it again. The measure rewards behaviour rather than the desired world state. Measure the proportion of floor area clean, averaged over eight hours, with a penalty for energy consumed.
rubric: Explain eject-and-recollect gaming.
Define success over environment states.
Include averaged clean area, eight hours and energy penalty.
questions.hint2: Rewarding dirt collected over eight hours encourages ejecting collected dirt and collecting it again.

questions.question: Write the rice-leaf classifier's complete PEAS specification from the handout, including refusal.
questions.modelAnswer: Performance: balanced accuracy across disease classes, false-negative rate on the most damaging disease, and latency under four seconds on a mid-range phone. Environment: variable daylight, wet leaves, motion blur, different camera quality and one or more leaves per frame. Actuators: displayed class label with confidence, recommended action and refusal at low confidence. Sensors: camera image, optionally device location and timestamp.
rubric: Include all four PEAS headings.
Include balanced accuracy, damaging-disease false negatives and latency.
Describe field conditions and camera inputs.
Include refusal as an actuator.
questions.hint2: Performance: balanced accuracy across disease classes, false-negative rate on the most damaging disease, and latency under four seconds on a mid-range phone.

questions.question: Compare the four principal architectures and explain what each addition provides.
questions.modelAnswer: Simple reflex agents use current-percept condition-action rules without memory, and can loop under partial observability. Model-based reflex agents add internal state and a model of world evolution and action effects, but the model may drift. Goal-based agents represent desirable states and search for an action sequence, adding flexibility at a speed cost. Utility-based agents map states to real values and maximise expected utility, handling conflicting objectives and uncertain outcomes.
rubric: Explain current percept versus internal state.
Explain model drift and partial observability.
Contrast binary goals with utility trade-offs.
Include search cost and expected utility.
questions.hint2: Simple reflex agents use current-percept condition-action rules without memory, and can loop under partial observability.

questions.question: Explain how each PEAS heading constrains a project's design and evaluation.
questions.modelAnswer: The performance measure becomes the evaluation metric; plain accuracy is misleading with imbalanced classes. The environment becomes the data-collection plan, so variable lighting requires corresponding images. Actuators become the interface and determine whether abstention is allowed. Sensors determine the feature set; every feature must be derivable from the listed sensors.
rubric: Map every heading to its downstream design choice.
Explain imbalanced classes and variable lighting.
Explain abstention and sensor-derived features.
questions.hint2: The performance measure becomes the evaluation metric; plain accuracy is misleading with imbalanced classes.
